zone.objective_why: data/rift_zones.json pass.objective_prefix is cob_pass_ and its zones are cob_pass_z1..z5, so cob_pass_relic is the same convention and collides with none of them. Per player, set to 1 once, never unset.
zone.fail_closed: the score is NOT tested inside the advancement. minecraft:entity_scores does not match when the objective has no value for that player, which is every player who has never stood at the HQ door, so a score condition in the advancement would fail OPEN. The advancement tests LOCATION only and the reward function tests the score with `execute unless score @s cob_pass_relic matches 1..`, which is true for an unset score. Copied verbatim in shape from data/rift_zones.json pass.fail_closed, which records the same bug being found and fixed.
zone.exempt_why: creative and spectator are never turned back, as data/gulch_mine.json's gate and data/rift_zones.json exempt do it: an operator inspecting the hall must not be bounced out of it
zone.y_why: THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THIS ZONE DIFFERS FROM EVERY ZONE BEFORE IT, and the difference is forced. data/rift_zones.json y and data/gulch_mine.json zone.y are both the full column, y-64 to y575, because flying over or digging under a surface zone is still inside it. A full-height relic zone cannot work: its columns lie under the relic area's own walkable surface, which zone z2 already admits at 8 badges, so every eight-badge player standing on the lip would be turned back by this zone. The top is y40: the hall's dome apex is y34 and the choked shaft stops at y40. The lowest ground anywhere over the zone's boxes is y86 (measured, x3419 z3312), so there are 46 blocks of rock between the zone's ceiling and the lowest surface over it, and no walking, flying or building player is ever inside it.
zone.y_what_it_gives_up: a player who tunnels down to y41 directly over the hall is NOT inside the zone and is not turned back. They are inside 46 blocks of rock, and the 24-block shell holds no natural void they could have arrived through; the last 6 blocks before the hall's apex are the choked shaft, which is rock. So the zone's ceiling is not a hole in it, but it IS a bound, and the bound is a deliberate trade for not turning back players on the surface.
zone.boxes_why: three rectangles, not a rasterised polygon: the carve is three rectangles. Box 1 is the hall's footprint bbox (3369-3411, 3241-3283) grown 3 for its wall; box 2 the gallery grown 3; box 3 the passage grown 2, from the cradle's doorstep (x3357) to two blocks short of the HQ doorway. The three boxes contain every cell this build carves and nothing else.
zone.threshold_why: the carve reaches x3421, the doorway, and the zone's boxes stop at x3419. The two columns between them, x3420 and x3421, are carved and deliberately OUTSIDE the zone: a player without the pass stands IN the open doorway, sees the passage running west and the light at the end of it, and is turned back the moment they step past x3420. That is the owner's sentence made visible instead of merely enforced. tools/relic_underground.py report treats any carved column west of this x outside the boxes as a hole in the zone and only these two as the threshold; the check FOUND these six columns (x3420-3421, z3305-3307) before this key existed.
boxes_do_not_include: the HQ basement (the records room, x3422-3428 at y0, geometry.hq.basement): the boxes' east limit is x3419, so the basement and the stair above it are OUTSIDE the zone and need no gate of their own
the cradle (x3357 and west): Codex's chamber and Codex's zone
the 24-block shell ring: it is solid rock, and widening the zone into it would reach under the lip where nothing is ours

pass.granted_at: the knock box, inside the HQ basement, immediately east of the open west doorway
pass.why: the pass IS 'you came through the Compact HQ'. It is granted only by standing in the HQ basement at the doorway, which is the owner's sentence in one mechanism: the route is the gate, and the zone check is what stops every other route. The eight badge flags are the second half of the test so that a passless player who reaches the basement before the eighth badge is still refused; they are the per-player advancements tools/progression_pack.py writes when rctmod counts each leader beaten (EXP-027), and they are the only flags in this design with a setter that exists.
pass.why_not_the_finale_flag: DEEP_CITY.md section 5 opens the cradle's check on the quest stage rift_crisis_pending and stands the cordon down on rift_crisis_resolved. NEITHER IS AVAILABLE TO AN ADVANCEMENT TODAY. rift_crisis_pending is a value of the quest field quest.main_worldshift_reveal.stage (data/progression.json), set by the dialogue transition record_rift_crisis_pending (data/quests.json, reached from dialogue node rift_007); it is not an advancement, and tools/progression_pack.py's flag advancements are a different mechanism. rift_crisis_resolved has NO SETTER ON ANY BRANCH (data/quests.json says so itself, and data/rift_zones.json zones.z5.needs_progression records the same). THIS FILE INVENTS NEITHER. The upgrade, when a setter exists, is one field: see needs.upgrade_path.
pass.never_unset: the pass is set once and never unset, like every cob_pass_*. So a player who has legitimately walked the HQ once may later arrive by any route. That is the same property z1-z5 have and is accepted on the same ground: the pass records that the player earned passage, not where they are standing.

knock.where: the records room's (the HQ basement's) west end, at the open doorway (x3421) the passage leaves by: x3422-3424 z3305-3307, feet at y1 on the room's floor y0. Carved air since 2026-10-02 (geometry.hq.basement); report and the audit both check every cell of it is air with a floor under it
knock.why: data/gulch_mine.json gate.knock and tools/rift_zones.py's knock boxes: a player standing in front of the way in is asking to be let through, so something answers. Here there is no guard and no grille, so the alcove itself is the asking. It is OUTSIDE the zone's boxes (which stop at x3419), so no exclusion arithmetic is needed and the knock and zone advancements can never fire on the same tick and race, which is the fault tools/rift_zones.py had to engineer around.

doorway.state: OPEN. No door, no bars, no seal, nothing to break and nothing to pick.
doorway.why: the owner: 'turned back by the zone check rather than barriers'. An open doorway with a zone behind it is the instruction exactly: the player can see the passage, can walk at it, and is turned back by the check and not by a block. It also deletes the dependency DEEP_CITY.md section 5 carried: a lumymon:elevator with requiredAdvancement set on the shaft. THAT FIELD IS ASSUMED, NOT SOURCED (DEEP_CITY.md cites it; no jar read or documentation is quoted anywhere in this repository), and this design does not need it: the shaft down from ring 0 can be plain stairs or an ungated lift, because the gate is not the shaft.

turn_back.spawnpoint_reset: a bed or respawn anchor set inside the zone is overridden first (`spawnpoint @s` for non-creative players) before the teleport, so a respawn cannot loop: RIFT_ZONES.md section 4 and tools/rift_zones.py turn_back.
turn_back.message: Turned back: the relic hall is reached through the Compact's HQ.

driver.why: no tick driver, deliberately. The check is advancement-driven, as data/gulch_mine.json's is and as tools/reapply.py's step table says of the gulch: 'the gate, the zone check ... act on their own and need no step'. The pack's only load-time work is creating one objective. This key records the deliberate absence so a later reader does not add a driver to a system that does not want one.

state_model.where_state_lives: one dummy scoreboard objective, cob_pass_relic, one value per player, created by the pack's load function and never reset by it. Nothing is stored server-wide; nothing is stored in the world beyond the blocks.
state_model.why_not_an_advancement: the pass could have been an advancement, and is not: the advancements in this system are the location triggers, which are granted and revoked every time they fire. Mixing a durable flag into a revoked-every-tick advancement set is how you lose it.
state_model.late_join: a player who joins after the others have been to the hall has no score, so has no pass. They walk the HQ themselves. Nothing about the hall's blocks is per-player, so the room they walk into is the room the others left.
state_model.death_inside: the turn-back resets the spawnpoint before teleporting, so a bed or anchor placed inside cannot loop a passless player. A player WITH the pass who dies inside respawns wherever their spawnpoint is and walks back in; the check never touches them.
state_model.disconnect_inside: the location advancement re-fires within a second of login (RIFT_ZONES.md section 4: 'the location test runs within a second of login'). A passed player stays; a passless one is turned back to ring 0.
state_model.different_order: the pass depends on eight badges and on standing at one doorway. It has no ordering with the cradle, the finale, the shrine's contents or any other zone, so two players at different points in the story reach it at their own pace with no shared state between them.
state_model.one_player_cannot_carry_another: the grant is `@s` inside the knock box, so only the player standing there is granted. A passed player walking west ahead of a passless one does nothing for the one behind: the one behind is turned back at x3419.
state_model.multiplayer_cost: one location test per player per second against three boxes. Negligible, and an order of magnitude cheaper than z1-z5, which test a few hundred boxes each.
state_model.no_server_wide_state: no shared flag, no global counter, no first-player-wins. The hall's own contents, if a Hoopa actor is ever put in it, are the scene runtime's per-player actors (DEEP_CITY.md section 5, EXP-034) and are not this file's.
state_model.release_per_player: the binder (geometry.release) is one shared, static NPC; what it changes is per player. Its dialogue reads and writes the TALKING player's Cobblemon player data (quest.main_worldshift_reveal.stage), and the transition's grant runs `advancement grant @s` as and at that player only (tools/compile_dialogue.py's `function` effect: execute as <their uuid>). Two players release Hoopa twice, each for themselves; a late joiner, a player who died, or one who disconnected mid-conversation is re-offered the choice while their own stage is still rift_crisis_pending, and a re-grant is a no-op. A player who released and comes back gets the after-release line.
